Quick update after audit of the event metadata:

- The original event was created by Finova's calendar (demo@finovabeta.com) and then forwarded; Exchange forwarding stripped the "conference" payload so some clients only saw attachments.
- Best practice in this case is to: 1) create the event from the hosting party's calendar (Redwood) and 2) include the direct link in both the calendar body and the email text. That avoids client-specific parsing differences.
- If Finova wants to retain organizer ownership (preferred by their security team), we can do an organizer swap: Redwood will create the Zoom meeting, then Finova's demo@finovabeta.com can be set as the organizer in the calendar event (we'll pass ownership via invite acceptance). That usually preserves SSO host eligibility.

Proposed final plan (action items):
- Ben: keep the Zoom meeting you created and enable co-hosts (done).
- Karthik: send a one-line calendar update from your Redwood calendar that embeds the Zoom URL in the body and subject; include Finova's demo@finovabeta.com as organizer if they confirm they want ownership.
- Sam: confirm whether Finova prefers organizer -> Redwood or Redwood -> Finova (ownership). If Finova wants to be organizer, provide the exact calendar account to put in the organizer field.

I'll standby to recreate the event as needed — want to avoid more forwards that strip metadata.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
